text:
Ravi (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock the private-deploy network modes for the Q3 shipping milestone. Field teams keep asking for IP preservation and a low-touch installer. Two candidate paths: 1) customer-managed routing (bgp/peering + IP preserve) 2) relay/egress-proxy mode (no peering, simpler ops). Need rollout sequencing, upgrade story, and clear consumer docs by end of month.
Joao (Eng): +1. Technical tradeoffs: customer-managed gives best performance/cost for tenants but huge variance in support. Relay mode simplifies install and keeps control plane isolated but adds latency and egress cost.
Maya (Solutions): Field feedback: top-tier customers demand preserved IPs for firewall allowlists. Mid-market prefers relay to avoid NetOps signoffs. We should support both, but make the default the low-touch relay.
Chris (SRE): From infra side, relay reduces blast radius for control plane upgrades. But we need an SLA-reconciliation plan: customers on relay must be warned about ~100-200ms tail for cross-region traffic.
Joao (Eng): Proposal: Phase A (GA): ship relay mode as default with an opt-in tenant-preserve feature that requires operator approval and explicit preflight checks. Phase B (next quarter): add automated BGP peering templates + operator wizard to enable preserve at scale.
Ravi (PM): Sounds reasonable. What about upgrade compatibility? If a customer flips preserve on later, how do we handle rolling upgrade and ip conflicts?
Joao (Eng): We'll require image-compatibility checks and BGP drain window. Rough flow: preflight -> dry-run peering -> ephemeral cutover with traffic mirroring -> finalize. If preflight fails, rollback to relay.
Maya (Solutions): Add a checklist for field: netops contact, CIDR reservation confirmation, firewall rules text to share with customer. I'll draft.
Chris (SRE): Implementation notes: need health probes for operator bridge + metrics for egress tail latency. Suggest adding a new SLI: "egress_tail_95p_ms" per tenant.
Ravi (PM): Good. Can we get a minimal install snippet for the relay default so we can include in quickstart?
Joao (Eng): Sure, minimal installer example for relay:
```bash
./redwood-installer --mode=relay --operator-version=1.2.0 --region=us-west-2 
# optional: --egress-proxy-size=small
```
Maya (Solutions): And for preserve (opt-in) we need a preflight CLI flag:
```bash
./redwood-installer --mode=preserve --preflight-only --reserved-cidrs=10.0.0.0/24
```
Joao (Eng): Note: preserve requires operator privileges and a runbook step to apply peering config. We'll gate behind a feature flag for the GA rollout.
Ravi (PM): Action items: 1) Joao: spec preflight + dry-run flow (due in 5 working days). 2) Maya: draft field checklist and sample firewall text (due in 3 working days). 3) Chris: define egress SLI and instrumentation plan (due in 7 working days). 4) I'll prepare comms and default policy language.
Alice-bot: Reminder scheduled: "private-deploy-network-handoff" on 2024-07-15 16:00 UTC.
Joao (Eng): One more ask — compatibility matrix for older operator versions. I'll add a short section: preserve mode requires operator >=1.2.0; relay works back to 1.0.x but with degraded metrics.
Maya (Solutions): Also recommend a customer-facing toggle with clear warnings: "Turning on preserve may require a maintenance window and NetOps coordination." I'll draft wording.
Ravi (PM): OK locking this thread as the canonical decision log for the moment. If anything changes post-spec review we update here. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
